name: A Madras Currie
author: Source author unknown
steps: Skin a fowl and cut it up into small joints
Fry it in butter a light brown
Put it into a saucepan with two tablespoonfuls of currie powder, the juice of a lemon, half a cocoa nut finely grated, a teaspoonful of salt, a little fried onion, and a clove of garlic
Let it simmer slowly for three hours, adding a thickening of butter and flour, just before it is sufficiently cooked

name: A Relish
author: Source author unknown
steps: Take of cayenne, ground ginger, black pepper, cinnamon and mace each one quarter of an ounce
of white pepper and grated nutmegs one ounce, and half a teaspoonful of ground cloves
mix well and put into a bottle
it will be found a great addition to soups and gravies, and mixed with a little vinegar to form a paste will make a delicious sauce for cold meat, steaks, &c.

name: Aadi Pilaw
author: Turabi Efendi
ingredientsText: a pound of the best rice, well washed
half a pound of fresh butter
steps: Pour two pints of water in a saucepan, and put it on the fire
When boiling, throw in a pound of the best rice, well washed, and sufficient salt, and boil it until the whole of the liquid is absorbed
Put in a saucepan half a pound of fresh butter, and set it on the fire until it boils
Pour it all at once over the rice, put the cover over the pan, wrap a wet cloth round it, to prevent the steam from escaping, and keep it on the hob for half an hour
Take the lid off and stir it once round with a fork
Dish up in the shape of a dome, and serve hot

name: Aletria Caseira (Homemade Aletria)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Make a dough with wheat flour, five eggs and a little salt
Beat well until it shows air bubbles when cut
Unroll the dough on a cloth and when well extended and thin, roll it up on itself
Cut the roll into very fine strips

name: Ante de Mamey (Mamey Paste Dessert)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Grind the mamey and add it to the syrup at medium point for six boilings
Add white wine, spices, raisins, almonds, and sesame seeds
Pour over sponge cake

name: Azas de Peru Fritas (Fried Turkey Wings)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Take the turkey wings and neck and cook in water with salt, parsley, and onion leaves
When cooked, remove the bones and cut the meat into small pieces
Beat with six eggs
Fry in lard
When fried, serve

name: Bacalao en Ajo Blanco sin Chile (Cod in White Garlic Sauce without Chile)
author: Mariano Galván Rivera
steps: Toast a piece of bread in the fire until half burnt, and grind it with garlic browned in lard and a little pepper.
Burn oil in a pan and brown there some chopped garlic cloves, add the ground bread with everything else, and the already-cooked cod, cut into slices.
sourceTitle: Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano

name: Baked Rice
author: Source author unknown
steps: Mix well rice, cheese in small bits, milk, eggs, butter and salt.
Place in baking dish with cheese and a little butter on top.
Bake half an hour.

name: Bakers' Bread
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: Flour Sufficient to Make a Smooth Dough
steps: Allow one ounce of Compressed Yeast to one quart of lukewarm water, and mix well in a wooden bread trough.
Then add flour enough to make a nice smooth dough of medium degree, not too stiff, nor yet too soft.
Work it well, and then let it stand for about five hours in a warm place so as to rise well.

When it drops, or begins to fall (you can tell this by watching the sides of the dough), add the same amount of water that was used in making the dough, putting two teaspoonfuls of salt into the water before adding it.

Work this well, and then throw down on the table, cut and mold the dough into loaves of whatever length is desired, and take a smooth stick and press lightly down across the loaf about two inches from the edge.
Put the loaves into the oven without setting in a pan.
Watch carefully, and see that the oven is of the proper temperature.
By following these directions, you will have nice, fresh, sweet New Orleans Bakers' Bread.

name: Beef or Mutton Baked with Potatoes
author: Source author unknown
steps: Boil some potatoes.
Peel and pound them in a mortar with one or two small onions.
Moisten them with milk and an egg beaten up.
Add a little salt and pepper.
Season slices of beef or mutton chops with salt and pepper, and more onion, if the flavour is approved.

Rub the bottom of a pudding-dish with butter, and put in a layer of the mashed potatoes, which should be as thick as a batter, and then a layer of meat, and so on alternately, till the dish is filled, ending with potatoes.
Bake in an oven for one hour.

name: Beefsteak with Oysters
author: Source author unknown
steps: Put oysters with very little of the juice into stew-pan.
When they come to a boil, remove the scum.
Stir in butter mixed with flour.
Let boil one minute until it thickens.
Pour over the steak.
Serve hot.

name: Beshmi
author: E.P. Veerasawmy
steps: Mix 1 powa of ghee thoroughly with 1 seer of besam of grams and heat
Stir constantly
Add 1 seer of ghee more in 2 or 3 instalments
Add 1 powa of sugar when the besam is fried red
Take down when it is thoroughly mixed up
Mix with 1 tola of powdered pepper
Powdered garam-masalla may also be added if desired
Make balls while the mass is yet warm

name: Boiled Potatoes
author: Christian Woman's Exchange
steps: Put potatoes in just water enough to cover them, with the skins on
Boil them constantly till done
Squeeze them in a dry cloth
Send them to the table very hot

name: Bolinhos de Manteiga (Butter Balls)
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: bread the size of two closed hands
steps: Soak bread the size of two closed hands in hot milk
When softened, remove it and knead with three tablespoons of wheat flour, four egg yolks and two egg whites, little salt, half a tablespoon of sugar and one tablespoon of butter
Form small balls with this mixture, boil them in water that is already boiling
Serve with meat broth or egg sauce

name: Brisket Stewed
author: Judith Cohen Montefiore (attr.)
ingredientsText: about six or seven pounds of brisket of beef
steps: Take about six or seven pounds of brisket of beef
Place it in a stewpan with only enough water to cover it
Season with a little spice tied in a bag
When the meat is tender and the spices sufficiently extracted to make the gravy rich and strong, part of it must be removed to another saucepan
Have ready a variety of vegetables cut into small shapes, such as turnips, carrots, mushrooms, cauliflowers, or whatever may be in season
Stew them gently till tender in the gravy
Glaze the meat and pour the gravy in the dish
Arrange the vegetables round

name: Capirotada de Nabos (Capirotada with Turnips)
author: Mariano Galván Rivera
steps: Cook turnips in salted water with garlic.
Make the sauce with broth poured over a mixture of ground garlic with cooked and ground chickpeas.
Layer in this order: bread toasts, turnips, slices of cooked ham, and cooked whole chickpeas.
Do not use cheese.
When sufficiently thickened, cover with breadcrumbs, add salt, pepper and burnt butter on top.
Place a hot griddle on top to brown it.
sourceTitle: Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano

name: Chicken Chop Sooy (With Giblets)
author: Jessie Louise Nolton
ingredientsText: One pound lean young pig pork, cut into slices one inch long, one-quarter inch wide and one-quarter inch thick
Two chicken livers, gizzards and hearts, sliced thin
One pound cooked white meat of chicken, cut fine
One small can white mushrooms, sliced
steps: Cut one pound lean young pig pork into slices one inch long, one-quarter inch wide and one-quarter inch thick.
Slice thin two chicken livers, gizzards and hearts, and one-half ounce green ginger roots.
Put all in kettle with one tablespoon olive oil previously heated, and brown evenly, stirring frequently till done, using care that it does not scorch.
Add one pound cooked white meat of chicken cut fine.
Pour around sides of kettle one cupful hot chicken stock, add one tablespoon Seasoning Sauce and stir carefully.
Have ready two cups celery cut fine, one small can white mushrooms sliced, a tablespoon shredded onion and put all in kettle, cooking for twelve minutes.
Put in one-half cup bean sprouts, adding a little as directed.
sourceTitle: Chinese Cookery in the Home Kitchen

name: Chicken Fruit Chop Sooy (Sum Soo)
author: Jessie Louise Nolton
ingredientsText: One-half pound lean pork from the shoulder
One-half pound white meat of cooked chicken
Six Chinese mushrooms, previously steamed with stems removed
One cupful weak and hot chicken stock
One dessertspoon rice flour, wheat flour, or cornstarch
steps: Cut fine one-half pound of lean pork from the shoulder, one-half pound white meat of cooked chicken, seven Chinese potatoes, six Chinese mushrooms, scant cupful bamboo shoots, and one cupful celery.
Place pork in kettle with one level tablespoon olive oil already heated to prevent meat from sticking, and stir frequently till done.
Add the cooked chicken meat and the vegetables prepared as directed above, adding a little more oil if necessary.
Draw the mixture carefully from the sides of the kettle to the center and pour around the sides of the kettle a cupful of weak and hot chicken stock.
Cover tightly and let cook slowly till the vegetables are done for about fifteen minutes.
Mix one teaspoon of each sauce with one dessertspoon rice flour, wheat flour, or cornstarch, a teaspoon chicken stock, and a pinch sugar to thicken gravy.
Add a little more stock to the kettle if necessary.
Serve with bowl of rice and pot of tea.
sourceTitle: Chinese Cookery in the Home Kitchen

name: Chinese Chop Sooy (Ordinary)
author: Jessie Louise Nolton
ingredientsText: A dessertspoonful of lard, olive oil, butter or peanut oil
One cupful hot chicken stock or water
Six Chinese mushrooms, soaked or steamed with stems removed
Six Chinese potatoes, peeled and sliced thin
A heaping teaspoon rice flour or cornstarch
steps: Cut one pound of lean pork in small pieces and braise in the kettle with a dessertspoonful of lard, olive oil, butter or peanut oil, the latter being preferred.
Cover tightly, removing the cover and stirring occasionally till cooked through and lightly browned.
Watch carefully to prevent burning.
Add one small cupful sliced onions and continue to cook for three or four minutes.
Pour a cupful of hot chicken stock or water, carefully around the sides of the kettle, taking great care not to pour over the top of the food.
Cut the Chinese mushrooms fine and the Chinese potatoes into thin slices.
Add the mushrooms, potatoes, and celery immediately to the pork and onions.
Put in one tablespoon of the Seasoning Sauce and mix well with the ingredients and cover the kettle tightly.
Let cook for twelve or fifteen minutes slowly, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking to bottom of kettle and burning.
Add water or stock, as necessary, to prevent the mixture from becoming dry.
Mix two tablespoons of the Flavoring Sauce with a heaping teaspoon of rice flour or cornstarch and add to the ingredients in the kettle, allowing the gravy to thicken slowly.
Add four drops of Sesamun Oil, stir carefully and remove from the fire.
Serve with rice in separate bowls and with tea.
sourceTitle: Chinese Cookery in the Home Kitchen

name: Chinese Sponge Cake
author: Shiu Wong Chan
ingredientsText: A few drops of lemon juice
steps: Beat the eggs in a suitable bowl. Mix well with sugar. Beat for an hour, being careful always to beat in one direction.
Mix with the flour and lemon juice.
Put into a suitable pan and steam for 3/4 hour.

name: Chocolate Caramels
author: Source author unknown
steps: Put all but the chocolate in a kettle and boil fast.
When it will almost thread, add chocolate.
Pour in buttered tins.
Cut when cold.

name: Chow Mein
author: Jessie Louise Nolton
steps: Do not allow the noodles to become too dry after making
If too much time is needed, place noodles in ice box till ready
Put olive oil in pan having the oil about one inch deep when heated
Spread the noodles over bottom of pan and let fry slowly till a golden color
Turn over with wide bladed knife or pancake turner and let fry on the other side till done, perhaps ten to fifteen minutes
Remove noodles and drain carefully to remove oil
Put on platter and serve with any one of the Chop Sooy dishes preferred
The Chop Sooy must be ready and hot, and the noodles served immediately when done
sourceTitle: Chinese Cookery in the Home Kitchen

name: Chutney, No. 1
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: half a pound or a little more of raisins stoned and cut in halves
about twenty chilies well pounded in a mortar
a quarter of a pound of fine ginger
a quarter of a pound of salt or not quite as much
one pound of brown sugar previously boiled to a syrup, or the same quantity of treacle or golden syrup
steps: Put into a large basin or pan, half a pound, or a little more, of raisins stoned and cut in halves, two onions, one garlic, one eschalot, and about twenty chilies well pounded in a mortar
add half a pound of mustard, a quarter of a pound of fine ginger, and a quarter of a pound of salt, or not quite as much
peel and slice one pound of sour apples, put them in a jar with a pint of vinegar
cover the jar well, and put it into the oven and bake until the apples are rather soft

When they are cold, add them to the other ingredients with one pound of brown sugar previously boiled to a syrup, or the same quantity of treacle or golden syrup, and about three pints of vinegar, including the quantity the apples were baked in
Stir all the ingredients well together, and bottle for use

name: Chutney, No. 2
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: a quarter of a pound of pudding raisins
a quarter of a pound of apples
the same quantity of moist sugar
chopped tomatos from which you have taken the seeds
steps: Stone and cut up into rather large pieces, a quarter of a pound of pudding raisins

add to these, a quarter of a pound of apples chopped in small pieces, the same quantity of moist sugar, and chopped tomatos from which you have taken the seeds, two ounces of tamarinds, a tablespoonful of salt, ditto of cayenne, a teaspoonful of ground ginger, two large onions chopped fine, very little chopped lemon peel, a pint of lemon juice, and one quart of vinegar
mix all these ingredients well together
then put them into a jar, well covered
Stir the mixture every day for four or five weeks
if at the end of that time it is too thin, pour enough of the liquid away to make it of a proper thickness, but not dry
bottle the chutney in bottles or jars for use

name: Claret Cup
author: Source author unknown
steps: Dissolve the sugar and lemon juice
Add the Claret, Curacoa, Brandy and sliced orange and lemon juice
Put to cool

name: Climbing Fish with Cabbage
author: E.P. Veerasawmy
ingredientsText: cabbage 1 medium sized or 2 to 2.5 seers chopped
steps: Prepare the climbing fishes, keep entire and fry in oil.
Take out the green peas from its legumes and fry them with pieces of potatoes and cassia leaves in ghee or oil.
Chop the tender white portion of the cabbage and fry it with ghee or oil till light brown.
Then add the potatoes, peas, fishes, all the spices pasted together and salt.
Water will come out of the vegetables when salt is added but a little more water may be necessary to boil them.
Season the curry with ghee boiled with a pinch of panch-foron, cassia leaves and chillies.
Add pasted garam-masalla before taking down.

name: Cocoa Nut Cakes
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: two or three ounces sifted white sugar
steps: Grate a fresh cocoa nut, and leave it to dry
Add to it a few sweet almonds and one bitter almond, also grated, two or three ounces of sifted white sugar, and sufficient well-beaten white of egg to make the whole into a stiff paste
Roll it into round balls
Bake on a greased tin until they are quite dry, and the top of them slightly browned
Put them off on to a cold dish

name: Cream Puffs
author: Christian Woman's Exchange
steps: Put 1 cup of water on the fire
When hot melt in 1 cup of best butter
When it boils beat in 1 cup of sifted flour
If lumpy, stir until perfectly smooth
Place it aside to cool
When cool, stir in 1 at a time 3 eggs without first beating them
Drop the batter on tins in small spoonfuls
Bake 1 hour in quick oven
For the cream put 1 1/2 cups of milk to boil
Beat yolks of 2 eggs very light with 4 tablespoonfuls of powdered sugar
When the milk boils, pour it on the eggs, stirring all the while
Wet 2 tablespoonfuls of cornstarch in fine flour with a little cold milk
Add it to the custard and replace on the fire
Stir until quite thick
Flavor when cold with vanilla
Place the cream in the puff by lifting up the top with a knife and dropping in the cream with a small spoon

name: Creamed Codfish
author: Source author unknown
steps: Pick apart codfish
Wash thoroughly in two waters
Soak over night in cold water
Next morning, drain, cover with boiling water and cook below the boiling point for five minutes
Drain and press
Rub butter and flour together
Add milk
Stir until boiling
Add a dash of pepper and the codfish
Cover and stand over hot water ten minutes
Add the beaten yolk of an egg and salt
Serve with plain boiled potatoes

name: Drawn Butter
author: Source author unknown
steps: Cut up butter and mix with flour.
Place in saucepan and add hot water.
Cover the pan and place in boiling water.
Move pan around continually in the same direction, till butter is entirely melted and begins to simmer.
Then let pan rest till it boils up.
If set on too hot a fire, contents will be oily.
If not well mixed, the butter and flour will be lumpy.
Avoid too much water.

name: Dried Shrimp Stew
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
ingredientsText: One and one half tablespoonfuls of syou
steps: Soak the shrimps in cold water for half an hour, drain, and cover with cold water, add the cayenne pepper and syou, and boil slowly about one hour.
Mix the rice flour with cold water to a smooth paste, and stir until it thickens.
Serve with rice.

name: Dry Pork On Rice
author: Shiu Wong Chan
steps: Wash the rice 3 times. Put in a covered pan with 7 cups of water and cook until done.
Place the pork on top of the rice. When dry remove to the back of the stove. Shake the pan frequently to prevent burning. Remove from the stove and keep the cover on for 10 minutes.
Take out the pork and cut into the required size.
Add salt and mix well.

name: Duck With Herbs
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
ingredientsText: One quarter pound of pork fat
steps: Drain and singe the duck.
Wipe, then thoroughly dry, inside and out, with a clean, damp cloth.
Line a pan with small pieces of pork (fat).
Sprinkle the bottom with minced onion, celery, grated lemon peel, and the garlic, grated fine.
Lay the duck in and cover with a tablespoonful of mixed spices, two tablespoonfuls of syou, and a cup of rich stock.
Set over the fire and simmer for two hours, basting often.
Wash the mushrooms and turn them in, and cook all together for ten minutes.
Take up, and thicken the gravy with cornstarch or rice flour.
Lastly, toss in the chopped parsley.
Cut up the duck in small pieces (not too small), arrange on dish, pour the gravy with the herbs around the duck, and serve hot with rice.

name: Egg and Olive Sandwiches
author: Florence Kreisler Greenbaum
steps: Chop four eggs which have been boiled fifteen minutes.
Add two tablespoons of chopped olives, season and moisten with olive oil and vinegar.
Spread between thin slices of buttered bread.

name: Ensalada de Coliflor (Cauliflower Salad)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Cook the cauliflower with salt
Fry chopped garlic in oil and butter
Add the cauliflower there and fry well
Place on a platter
Add oil, vinegar, olives, chiles in vinegar, chopped onion, a little salt, pepper, and a little Chinese oregano dusted on top

name: Extra White Chop Suey
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
ingredientsText: Breast of one and one half pound chicken
One half can of bamboo shoots
One and one half teaspoonfuls of salt
steps: Cut in small pieces the breast of a young chicken of about one and one half pounds.
Put a tablespoonful of chicken fat in a deep frying pan, and heat very hot, then put in the chicken and fry brown, stirring to keep from burning.

Have ready one pound of fresh white mushrooms, cut small; half a bunch of celery, chopped; a dozen water chestnuts, peeled and cut in slices; two white onions, and half a can of bamboo shoots, all sliced.
Add all these to the chicken, and cook for ten minutes.
Add two pounds of bean sprouts, and cook for another five minutes with two tablespoonfuls of syou and a dash of cayenne pepper.
Simmer for five minutes longer, and serve with rice.

name: Filled Lemons
author: Florence Kreisler Greenbaum
steps: Select good-sized lemons
cut off tip to stand the lemon upright
cut top for cover
Scoop out all the lemon pulp, and put in a bowl
put shells in a bowl of cold water
For six lemons take one box of boneless sardines, six anchovies, and two green peppers, cut very fine
Wet with lemon-juice until moist
fill in shells after wiping dry
insert a pimento on top
put on cover of lemon
serve on doily with horseradish and watercress

name: Fish Cofta Curry
author: Source author unknown
steps: Use cold boiled or fried fish which is best adapted for making coftas
Follow the instructions as already given at length in the foregoing recipes
Use mustard oil which is best adapted for fresh-fish curries

name: Foo Tay Dan (Chinese Ham and Eggs)
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
ingredientsText: one half cup of minced ham
one half of a small onion
steps: Heat one tablespoonful of ham fat very hot.
Chop up half a cupful of ham meat; slice thin half a dozen water chestnuts and half a small onion.
Fry all together for five minutes; then beat six eggs, turn in pan, and scramble.

name: Frango Guisado com Carapicú (Stewed Chicken with Carapicú)
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: one glass of wine or water
steps: Cook chicken cut into pieces with chopped bacon, salt, parsley, pepper, cloves of India, and onion
When cooked, remove it and strain the broth, reducing it by half
Add a handful of carapicús, juice of one bitter orange, one spoon of tapioca, one spoon of sugar, and three egg yolks mixed in one glass of wine or water
Bring the sauce to a boil, add the chicken pieces, finish cooking, and serve with simple cornmeal mush or with the sauce

name: Frango Refogado em Molho Branco (Chicken Braised in White Sauce)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Soak the chicken pieces in garlic wine for some time
Braise in hot butter until browned
Add one cup of water and one spoon of wheat flour
Add lemon juice and lemon slices
Let simmer until cooked
Thicken the sauce with two egg yolks and serve

name: Fricassee of Oysters
author: Source author unknown
steps: Drain and wash oysters.
Cook until the gills curl.
Drain, saving the liquor.
Add to it sufficient milk to make a pint.
Put butter and flour in a saucepan and mix.
Add liquor and milk, and stir until boiling.
Add salt, cayenne pepper and the oysters.
Heat over hot water.
Beat the yolks of eggs with cream.
Stir them quickly into the oysters.
Take from the fire, and serve on toast, or in a dish, garnished with triangular pieces of toast.
Sprinkle finely chopped parsley over the top.

name: Galinha d'Angola Cozida com Moranga (Guinea Fowl Boiled with Squash)
author: Source author unknown
steps: After plucking and cleaning the bird, boil it in water and salt with one squash cut into pieces with seeds removed
When cooked, remove the pieces of squash, place them on a plate with the skin facing down
Cut the bird into pieces and place them on the squash, drizzling melted butter over all and dusting with sugar
Place the plate in the oven, let it roast for half an hour, and serve

name: Haceb-Dolmassi
author: Turabi Efendi
ingredientsText: two or three tablespoonfuls of the inside of egg-plants
juice of two or three lemons
steps: Cut off the tops and take out the insides of half a dozen egg-plants
Put them in salt water for ten minutes or so

Mince fine a sufficient quantity of raw mutton, add one or two onions, a little mint, a small quantity of saffron, two or three tablespoonfuls of the inside of egg-plants, all chopped fine, a handful of well-washed rice, a little salt and pepper, mix them well all together with your hands
Stuff the egg-plants with it, and cover them with the tops
Lay some rib-bones of mutton on the bottom of a stewpan, and place the egg-plants over carefully
Cover them with broth, add the juice of two or three lemons
Set the pan on a charcoal fire with the cover over, and let it simmer until the egg-plants are soft, and a nice gravy is formed at the bottom
Dish them up carefully, and serve

name: Huevos Duros (Hard-Boiled Eggs)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Cook with shell and when hard remove and discard shell
Cut into slices and place on a plate
Serve with salt, oil, vinegar and pepper
These are usually served this way to garnish raw salads, plates of asparagus, cauliflower, etc.

name: Imitation Preserved Ginger
author: Source author unknown
steps: Make a syrup with one pound of loaf sugar to four pints of water
Peel a vegetable marrow, remove the seeds and pulp, and cut it into pieces two or three inches in length
Pour the syrup over the vegetable marrow, and let it remain two or three days
Drain it from the syrup, and to each pound of marrow add the juice of one

name: Inja-Burek
author: Turabi Efendi
ingredientsText: a pound and a half of flour
minced mutton or cheese or mushrooms
steps: Put a pound and a half of flour on a slab, make a hole in the centre, in which put a teaspoonful of salt and four eggs
Mix all together, then add sufficient water, and form it a softish flexible paste
Dip your hands into melted fresh butter, and work it for a few minutes longer

Divide it into thirty pieces the size of walnuts, sprinkle a little wheat-starch both under and over them, and roll them out one by one with a rolling-pin as thin as a wafer, or thinner than that if you can, and the size of the baking-tin you intend to lay them in

Butter the baking-tin, in which lay five of the pieces of paste one over the other, sprinkle a little fresh butter all over, and lay five more pieces over, butter again, and over which lay five more pieces, butter again

Lay all over either minced mutton, mixed with mushrooms and onions, both chopped very fine, and previously stewed a nice brown in fresh butter, together with the meat, or cheese, or any other ingredients you may fancy
Cover it with the remaining pieces of paste in the same way as before
Cut it in four crossways, pour a little hot fresh butter over, and bake it a nice brown in a moderate oven
When done, dish up and serve

name: J. P.'s Currie
author: Source author unknown
steps: Cut up a fowl into small joints and put it into a stewpan with two ounces of butter, and three sliced onions
Let it stew until the meat has acquired a nice brown colour, but do not allow it to get black
Add one pint of boiling stock
Mix one tablespoonful of currie powder and the same quantity of flour, with a little cold water into a smooth paste, and put this into the stewpan
Peel and slice two sour apples (taking out the core), which add to the fowl, and other ingredients
Let all stew gently, for at least an hour
Squeeze into it the juice of half a lemon and serve

name: Karefish Nigore (Sole Jelly)
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
ingredientsText: one half pound Kanton (dried seaweed jelly)
steps: First prepare the sole by cutting away the head and thoroughly cleaning and scaling.
Cut in fillets or slices, removing the small bones.
Take one cupful of mirin sauce and a pinch of salt.
Place in pot, and boil only a few minutes.
Chop into small pieces two carrots and about a quarter pound of dried mushrooms (first washed and soaked).
Boil in a small quantity of water, and when tender, strain.
Add the mirin sauce, previously boiled for fifteen minutes.
Wash half a pound of dry seaweed jelly, and soak in water for two hours.
Take out, and squeeze dry.
Break in small pieces, and throw in pan with a quart of water.
Boil and dissolve.
Strain into another saucepan.
Add half a cupful of sugar and a tablespoonful of syou sauce.
With this mix the fish and vegetables, and stir thoroughly.
Transfer to lacquered or smooth wooden box, and let it set.
When it is firm, cut in desired small shapes.

name: Kawun Bahlawdssi
author: Turabi Efendi
ingredientsText: fifteen or twenty pieces of paste (No. 135)
steps: Butter a baking-tin, in which lay fifteen or twenty pieces of paste (No. 135), sprinkling scalded fresh butter between each one
Peel a small musk-melon or any other sweet melon, cut it in two, take out the seeds
Mash one half or the whole of the melon with a wooden spoon
Lay it all over the paste half an inch thick
Cover it with fifteen or twenty pieces of paste as before
Bake it a nice colour
When done, and while hot, shake some powdered sugar over, and serve

name: Kebab Kyufte
author: Turabi Efendi
ingredientsText: two or three pounds of raw leg of mutton, beef, or veal
crumb of a French penny roll
two or three teacups of brown gravy
two or three teaspoonfuls of flour
steps: Put on a chopping board two or three pounds of either a raw leg of mutton, or beef, or veal, half a handful of parsley cleaned, two or three onions peeled, and the crumb of a French penny roll
Sprinkle a little salt, pepper, and cinnamon over, and mince them very fine together until like a paste
Make it up in shapes of small buns, or any shape you may fancy, and fry them a nice colour in fresh butter
Put two or three teacups of brown gravy in a saucepan, with two or three teaspoonfuls of flour, the juice of a lemon, and a little salt
Set it on a slow fire, and keep stirring until it is a nice consistency
Dish the meat up tastefully, and pour the gravy over, and serve hot, or serve it with finely sliced onions and chopped parsley over, instead of gravy, if approved of

name: Kid Curry
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: a hind-quarter or a fore-quarter of kid
steps: Cut the kid into sixteen or eighteen pieces
Take condiments in the proportion given in recipe No. 16
Cook it in every particular the same as the chicken curry
Allow it to simmer three-quarters of an hour

name: Kuru Silkme
author: Turabi Efendi
ingredientsText: three or four pounds of mutton
three or four ounces of fresh butter
steps: Cut three or four pounds of mutton into small pieces
Wash and dry them in a cloth, then place them in a stewpan with sufficient salt and pepper
Set it on the fire, and stir with a wooden spoon until it begins to hiss, which indicates that all the moisture is dispersed
Add three or four ounces of fresh butter, and keep stirring till the meat is nicely browned
When done, take them out with a hand-strainer, and place them in a dish
Keep it hot
Cut three or four egg-plants in thin slices, sprinkle them with salt, and let them remain for a few minutes
When the bitter juice is drawn from them, fry them a nice colour on both sides in the remaining fat from the meat
Arrange them tastefully over the meat, or round the dish, sprinkle a little pepper over, and serve hot

name: Lampreado de Tocino (Lampreado of Bacon)
author: Mariano Galván Rivera
steps: Choose very lean bacon shanks, put them to desalt a little, and cook them with pork loins; as soon as they are well cooked, remove them, let them cool and mince them.

Grind saffron, pepper, cinnamon, of each thing the proper amount, and a little toasted clove; incorporate everything with the paste, add raisins, almonds, pine nuts, and beat the paste with eggs in proportional quantity.

Make some small pastries and fry them with eggs, which will be well beaten, giving them two or three layers; put them in the syrup, which will have cinnamon, pepper, little clove and wine. If desired, a little vinegar, toasted sesame, raisins and almonds can be added.
sourceTitle: Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano

name: Lechugas Picadas en Leche (Chopped Lettuce in Milk)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Remove tough leaves and veins, wash well
Blanch in boiling salted water
Refresh in cold water
Drain and squeeze well
Chop as the previous recipe
Cook and prepare as for sorrel in milk
Generally nothing is placed on top

name: Leitão Assado no Espeto à Mineira (Spit-Roasted Suckling Pig Minas Style)
author: Source author unknown
steps: The suckling pig is cleaned and washed as was already explained above.
Split it into two halves, with one of them having the head, that is, cut lengthwise, rub it with salt and garlic, leave it in a marinade for twelve hours.
Thread each of these halves on a spit, passing the spit between the ribs and the skin.
As for the half where the head adheres, the point of the spit comes out through the mouth.
Tie the foot to the spit with a cord, and make a small hole in the skin into which the hand is inserted.
In this state, it goes to the oven, resting the point of the spit on a support which was proportioned.

name: Lemunyd Kdymaghi
author: Turabi Efendi
ingredientsText: a pound of strawberries or raspberries
three or four ounces of powdered sugar
two or three tablespoonfuls of water
an ounce and a half of melted isinglass
half a pint of the fruit
a few drops of the essence of rose or orange-flower
steps: Take off the stalks of a pound of strawberries or raspberries, wash and put them in a stewpan, with three or four ounces of powdered sugar, and two or three tablespoonfuls of water
Put the pan on a moderate charcoal fire, and boil till rather thick, stirring it at the same time with a wooden spoon
When cold, pass it through a sieve into a basin, add an ounce and a half of melted isinglass to half a pint of the fruit, and stir it well
Add a pint of whipped cream, with a few drops of the essence of rose or orange-flower; mix well all together
Pour it into a mould, and place it on ice, or in a cool place, until firm
When ready, turn it out and serve

name: Lord Clive's Currie
author: Source author unknown
steps: Take six sliced onions, one green apple, and a clove of garlic
Stew them to a pulp in a little good stock
Add one teaspoonful of currie powder, a few tablespoonfuls of stock, a salt-spoonful of salt, and the same quantity of Cayenne pepper
Add to this gravy any kind of uncooked meat cut into small pieces
Add a piece of butter

name: Lucauian Eggs
author: Source author unknown
steps: Cut eggs in eighths lengthwise.
Add cooked macaroni, cheese, and white sauce seasoned with salt, pepper, onion juice and anchovy essence.
Turn into a buttered baking dish; cover with buttered crumbs and set in the oven long enough to bake crumbs.

name: Mallard Ducks or Canvasback Ducks Roasted
author: Source author unknown
steps: Clean the ducks as you would a chicken, without scalding, however, rinse out the inside and wipe well inside and out with a wet towel.
Do not wash the duck unless you have broken the gall bladder, as the washing destroys their flavor.
Rub the inside well with salt and pepper, and rub outside as thoroughly.
Place a three-inch lump of butter on the inside.
Truss nicely and place the ducks in a baking pan, and brush the tops with melted butter.

Pour over two tablespoonfuls of water, and set in a very hot oven, and allow them to bake twenty minutes, if they are not very large, and thirty minutes, if larger than the ordinary size of Canvasback ducks.
A wild duck is never cooked dry. It must reach the point where the blood will not run if the flesh is pierced with the fork in carving.
When done, place the ducks in a very hot dish, and serve with their own gravy poured over them.
Garnish nicely with parsley or water cress.
Serve with Currant Jelly.
Always have the plates very hot in which you serve the ducks at table.

name: Marshmallow Cake
author: Source author unknown
steps: Bake angel cake in two layers
Make boiled icing of one large cup sugar to whites of two small eggs
Cut marshmallows in halves and put on coating of icing, then more icing
Flavor with two-thirds vanilla and one-third almond

name: Medkune
author: Turabi Efendi
ingredientsText: two or three pounds of mutton
juice of two or three small lemons
steps: Peel four or five egg-plants, cut them in slices about three-quarters of an inch thick, and partly scald them in salt water
Cut two or three pounds of mutton in pieces the size of walnuts, sprinkle one or two chopped onions over with a little salt, and rub them well together with your hands
Place into a stewpan the pieces of meat and the egg-plants, in layers, cover them with mutton or beef broth, add the juice of two or three small lemons
Put the pan on the fire with the lid on, and let it simmer until it forms a nice gravy at the bottom
Dish it up, sprinkle a little cinnamon over, and serve

name: Mulligatawny
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: the juice of a lime or small lemon
a piece of butter mixed with a little flour
steps: Cut up the fowl and put it into a pan with two quarts of cold water
Let it simmer until all the juice of the meat is extracted
Strain it, and when cold, put to the liquor two chickens, cut as for a fricassee

Add two tablespoonfuls of currie powder, one sliced onion and a clove of garlic, a little salt, the juice of a lime or small lemon, a piece of butter mixed with a little flour, and a wineglassful of Madeira
When ready to dish up, which will be in about three-quarters of an hour, throw in a little fried onion
Serve rice with it, but in another dish

name: Mutton Cutlets with Mixed Vegetables
author: Wyvern (A.R. Kenney-Herbert)
ingredientsText: eight cutlets from a neck of mutton
steps: Take the eight cutlets and trim them neatly
Grill them over a brisk, clear fire
When done, arrange them round a circle of nicely mashed potato
Place a sauce an macedoine de legumes in the centre
The sauce should contain French beans, a carrot, a turnip, and a piece of cucumber, previously boiled and cut into small dice
Heat the vegetables up in well made sauce blonde
Add a few green peas and some pieces of boiled celery if available

name: Nut Cake
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: 1 teaspoon soda dissolved in 3 tablespoons hot water
steps: Cream butter and sugar
Add eggs
Add flour
Add dates and walnuts
Dissolve soda in hot water and add
Bake

name: Orange Biscuits
author: Source author unknown
steps: Beat the eggs and sugar to a cream.
Add the flour gradually, and the juice and zest of the orange.
Beat well.
Bake on paper sheets, in the form of small wafers, very thinly spread, in a moderate oven, to a light color.

name: Orange Cream
author: Christian Woman's Exchange
steps: Take the juice of 4 oranges, and the rinds of 2, grated, the yolks of 8 eggs
Mix it well together and stir it over a chafing dish of coals
Add 1/2 a pint of cream, and stir it all one way

name: Partridge Hash
author: Shiu Wong Chan
steps: Cut the partridges, water chestnuts, mushrooms, and bamboo shoots into very small pieces. Cut the lettuce into threads.
Fry the chopped partridges in a hot, oiled pan.
Add the ginger juice and Fun Wine.
Add the vegetables and mix well.
Add enough primary soup to cover and cook until done.
Add Chinese gravy and remove from the stove at once. Salt to suit the taste.
Serve on top of the lettuce. Use the Chinese ham dice and fried noodles as a garnish.

name: Pastel de Queso (Cheese Pie)
author: Mariano Galván Rivera
steps: Make the pastry with real dough (without sugar)
When moistened with eggs, mix in grated cheese or cheese cut into pieces
Proceed as for other pastries
sourceTitle: Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano

name: Pdlude
author: Turabi Efendi
steps: Dissolve two pounds of white sugar in a stewpan with two quarts of water
Add about five ounces of wheat starch
Stir it well
When as smooth as milk, put it on a moderate charcoal fire
Continually stir it for about three hours, or until it forms a smooth substance, but not too thick
Add a few drops of the essence of rose or orange-flower
Stir it for a few minutes longer
Pour it into a mould previously oiled with almond-oil
Put it on ice, or in a cool place, till firm
When ready, dip the mould in warm water and turn it out
Serve (You can ornament the top with some skinned pistachios or almonds)

name: Perdizes, Codornizes, etc. Ensopadas com Guandús (Partridges, Quail, etc. Stewed with Pigeon Peas)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Brown one spoon of cornmeal flour with two spoons of fat
Add the bird cut into pieces and turn on all sides
Add a portion of pigeon peas cooked in water and salt
Stir and boil for another half hour
Add a glass of vinegar at the end and serve

name: Perú Assado com Pinhões (Roast Turkey with Pine Nuts)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Soak the turkey, brushed with salt, garlic, onion and lemon juice, for four hours.
Then fill it with cooked and peeled pine nuts, cut cooked eggs, half a dozen sliced bananas and peeled lemon slices without seeds.
Place it in a pan lined with bacon and roast it.
When cooked, serve it with its own sauce after removing the fat.

name: Pescoço de Carneiro Assado na Grelha (Grilled Lamb Neck)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Cut the neck meat into slices
Place over fire with cold water, salt, parsley, and onion leaves
Boil for half an hour
Remove and wrap with bread crumbs
Cover with a little melted butter
Roast on the grill
Serve with spicy sauce

name: Pickled Beef Tongue
author: Florence Kreisler Greenbaum
steps: Soak in cold water one-half hour.
Crush a piece of saltpetre, size of walnut, one teacup of salt, one teaspoon of pepper, three small cloves of garlic cut fine; mix seasoning.
Drain water off tongue.
With a pointed knife prick tongue; rub in seasoning.
Put tongue in crock; add the balance of salt, etc.; cover with plate and weight.
Allow to stand from four to five days.
Without washing off the seasoning, boil in fresh water until tender.

name: Postre de Yemas de Huevo, Bizcocho y Mantequilla (Dessert of Egg Yolks, Sponge Cake and Butter)
author: Mariano Galván Rivera
steps: Cook milk with sugar
Beat egg yolks and mix with the cooked milk
Take a cold slab of the best sponge cake and cut it into slices
In a dish, lay down a layer of slices and on top of each slice place layers of butter, adding cinnamon and toasted sesame seeds to each one, until filling the platter
Once well layered high, pour the milk with egg yolks over it until well soaked
Place fire above and below, both not too intense, and leave until it sets like a cake
Decorate with toasted sesame seeds and ground cinnamon on top
sourceTitle: Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano

name: Princess Royal Custard
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: quarter of a pound Jordan almonds
essence of almonds or orange-flower water
steps: Beat up in a large deep bowl the yolks of eight fresh eggs
Dredge into it while beating up a dessertspoonful of corn-flour
Sweeten to taste with the best pounded loaf sugar
Add to it a quarter of a pound of Jordan almonds well bruised in a marble mortar
Pour the mixture into a clean newly-tinned copper pan
Stir into it a seer of good cold milk
Put the pan on the fire
Never cease stirring it, keeping the spoon as much as possible in the centre of the pan
Reduce the flame after it has boiled for fifteen minutes, and continue to boil for a few minutes longer, until the custard is of the consistency required
Fill the custard cups or glasses, leaving about half an inch space to fill up with the whites of the eggs, beaten up to a very light froth
Flavour it with a little essence of almonds, or orange-flower water

name: Prunes a la Chasseur
author: Wyvern (A.R. Kenney-Herbert)
ingredientsText: glass jar of best French plums (prunes)
steps: Buy a glass jar of the best French plums (prunes) and a bottle of good cherry brandy
Take out a few plums
Pour as much cherry brandy into the jar as the plums will admit
The next day you can add more, for the plums will absorb the brandy
Continue for a day or two
Finally cork it down for a fortnight or so
Serve at dessert
Never let the jar be empty, but re-fill it as the plums are eaten

name: Pumpkin and Yellow Seeds
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
steps: Remove large seeds and spread them on paper.
Sprinkle with salt, and bake them until dry.

name: Risen Waffles
author: Source author unknown
steps: Scald the milk, add the butter, and let it grow tepid.
Sift the flour and salt together, and add the milk and butter, and finally the yeast.
Beat all continuously for five or ten minutes, and then cover well and set in a warm place for about two hours.
Beat the whites and the yolks of the eggs separately, and add first the yolks to the batter, after it has risen well, and then add the whites.
Beat in thoroughly, and set to rise again for about a quarter of an hour.
Then beat lightly and pour into a pitcher.
Prepare the waffle irons as indicated above, and proceed to bake in the same manner.

name: Roast Chicken (Japanese Style)
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
steps: Clean and singe the chicken.
Put the feet to boil until the scabs scale off, then place with the giblets to boil slowly.
Make a stuffing of rice boiled dry in chicken gravy, add chopped onion and a pinch of mixed spices, salt, pepper, and a dash of cayenne.
Put this in body of chicken and sew up.
Roast for an hour, or longer, according to age of chicken.
Make a gravy from the stock of the giblets.
Chop the giblets up fine and add to the gravy.
Serve with roasted sweet potatoes.

name: Sauce for Victoria Pudding
author: Wyvern (A.R. Kenney-Herbert)
steps: Mix flour with half an ounce of butter
Add a cupful of boiling water
Stir in jam, lime juice, and brandy
Simmer for five minutes
Mix with a little pat of butter
Strain and pour over and round the pudding

name: Sauer Kraut
author: Judith Cohen Montefiore (attr.)
ingredientsText: seven or eight pounds of beef, either brisket or a fillet off the shoulder
steps: Boil about seven or eight pounds of beef either brisket or a fillet off the shoulder in enough water to cover it
When it has boiled for one hour, add as much sauer kraut as may be approved
Let it stew gently for four hours
Serve in a deep dish
Remove the fat for a more delicate dish

name: Scalloped Potatoes, No. 2
author: Florence Kreisler Greenbaum
steps: Cut cold potatoes into cubes
Mix well with cream sauce, adding more seasoning if necessary
Pour into a baking dish
Cover with bread crumbs
Dot with small pieces of butter
Bake for about half an hour

name: Shark Fins
author: Shiu Wong Chan
ingredientsText: a few pieces of dry garlic
steps: Buy 2 pounds of dry shark fins from a Chinese grocery store. Soak in cold water for 3 hours.
Boil the fins with a few pieces of dry garlic and 2 pieces of ginger root. Change the water several times when boiling.
Put into a suitable pan. Add 2 tablespoonfuls of lard, and twice more than enough primary soup to cover. Boil slowly for 3/4 hour. Drain off the liquid and throw it away.
Put into another pan, containing 6 pints of primary soup, and boil.

Change again into a third pan of primary soup. Add gravy which consists of 1 cup of chicken starch, the whites of 3 eggs, Chinese ham dice and a little cornstarch and salt. Use 1 tablespoonful red vinegar to improve the taste. Garnish with parsley and serve hot.

name: Shrimps with Gourd Leaves
author: E.P. Veerasawmy
ingredientsText: chopped and thoroughly washed tender gourd leaves
steps: Prepare some lobsters, cut in pieces and fry.
Fishes are always to be smeared with powdered turmeric and salt before frying.
Then brown some potatoes and onions peeled and cut in pieces.
Add water, salt, powdered turmeric, cumin, pepper, chillies, coriander and some chopped and thoroughly washed tender gourd leaves.
When fully boiled season the curry with ghee or oil boiled with a few cassia leaves and panch-foron.
Garam-masalla may be added.
Leave little soup.

name: Steak Stewed with Tomatoes
author: Estella Atrutel
steps: Cut 3 or 4 good sized tomatoes and put them in a stewpan with an onion
Add salt and pepper
Put in the steak
As soon as it is tender take out the steak
Rub the tomatoes and onion through a sieve
Put back the steak in the saucepan and throw over the sauce
sourceTitle: An Easy and Economical Book of Jewish Cookery

name: Steamed Duck
author: Shiu Wong Chan
steps: Soak the chestnuts and barley in cold water for 1 hour.
Open the back of the duck with one cut about 4 inches long. Take out the bones without tearing the meat.
When the duck has been cleaned wash it inside and out with Chinese sauce. Salt thoroughly and put into a hot, oiled pan and fry for 10 minutes.
Add the Fun Wine. Turn the duck frequently.
Now put the duck, with the open side upward, in a bowl a little larger than the duck. Fill with the chestnuts, barley, and white nuts and any juice left in the frying-pan.
Steam for 2½ hours.
Pour off the gravy into another bowl. Skim off the oil.
Transfer the duck carefully into a larger bowl by holding the bowls mouth to mouth.
Pour the gravy over the duck and serve.

name: Stewed Onions
author: Source author unknown
steps: Cook as boiled onions; drain.
Add milk, butter, pepper and salt, flour stirred to a cream.
Let all boil up at once.
Serve.

name: Strawberries A La Bridge
author: Florence Kreisler Greenbaum
steps: Into a champagne-glass put large strawberries, halved and sugared, and an equal amount of marshmallows halved.
Place on top a mass of whipped cream, already sweetened and flavored.
Top with a single strawberry, sprinkle with shelled pecans.

name: Stuffed Bananas
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
steps: Bake long, plump bananas for ten minutes in medium oven.
Remove and split skin down one side.
Remove the inside, and whip it up with shredded coconut, a little cream and sugar, and a little lemon juice.
Return to shell, and bake for another ten minutes.

name: Stuffed Chicken (Turkish Style)
author: Florence Kreisler Greenbaum
steps: Steam chicken and when it is almost tender stuff it with the following: Take one-fourth pound of almonds, chopped; season with parsley, pepper and salt to taste, add one tablespoon of bread crumbs and bind this with one well-beaten egg.
Put chicken in roasting-pan and roast until done.

name: Stuffed Pig's Feet a la Perigueux
author: Source author unknown
steps: Boil the Pig's Feet, and then split them in two.
Take out the bones, lay the flesh on a dry, clean cloth and wipe well.
Make a forcemeat of boned turkey.
Add the truffles, which have been finely minced, and a half glass of Madeira or Sherry wine.
Mix this well together.
Take six pieces of crepinette, cut them the size of a man's hand and lay on a clean biscuit board.
Place on each piece of skin a portion of the forcemeat about the size of a hen's egg and flatten out well.
Place one-half of a pig's foot on top of this farcie, and cover with another layer of the stuffing.
On either side lay three thin slices of truffles.
Wrap the crepinettes up in some fanciful shape, such as an envelope or card case.
Dip them separately in a well-beaten egg, and then in grated bread-crumbs.
Put two tablespoonfuls of butter in a saucepan or deep frying pan, cover closely.
Let the feet cook on a slow fire for twenty-five minutes, allowing twelve minutes and a half to each side.
Serve with a pint of hot Perigueux sauce.
Place the sauce in a dish, lay the feet neatly over it and send to the table hot.

name: Sweet and Pungent Chicken
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
ingredientsText: Three and one half pound chicken
steps: Take a young chicken of about three and one half pounds.
Clean and singe it, and remove all the bones.
Lay in a stone dish and over it pour (enough to cover well) a mixture of two cupfuls of boiling vinegar, a dessert-spoonful of salt, and two tablespoonfuls of sugar.
Cover, and put away in a cool place for twenty-four hours.
Prepare a brown gravy by chopping half an onion and frying it a light brown in sweet lard or chicken fat.
Cut the chicken into quarters, and put in a pan with two tablespoonfuls of syou.
Simmer for half an hour very gently.
Serve with rice.

name: Tekir-Betlighi Pulalcissi
author: Turabi Efendi
ingredientsText: juice of one or two lemons
yolks of two or three eggs
a quarter of a pint of olive oil
steps: Take out the gills and the insides of seven or eight red mullets, and wash them
Peel two or three onions, and well pound them in a mortar
Add a little mixed spice, salt, and pepper, the juice of one or two lemons, the yolks of two or three eggs, and a little water, and beat them up well together with a wooden spoon
Pour it over the mullets, and let them remain for about two hours
Put a quarter of a pint of olive oil in a flat stewpan, with a plate of chopped parsley
Put it on the fire, and just scald it
Add half a pint of water, half a teaspoonful of salt
When it boils, lay the mullets in with the ingredients, and let it simmer for fifteen or twenty minutes
Dish up tastefully, and serve hot

name: Tendons of Veal
author: Judith Cohen Montefiore (attr.)
steps: Cut from the bones of a breast of veal the tendons which are round the front
Trim and blanch them
Put them with slices of smoked beef into a stewpan with some shavings of veal, a few herbs, a little sliced lemon, two or three onions, and a little broth
They must simmer for seven or eight hours
When done, thicken the gravy

name: The Pearl
author: Source author unknown
steps: Let the sugar boil a little longer

If you find that on drawing it out to a thread it snaps quickly, and also that while boiling the sugar presents the form of large pearls or globules on its surface, it will then have reached the small pearl degree
When the pearls become closely connected on the surface of the sugar, it will have reached the large pearl degree

name: To Boil Rice for Currie
author: Source author unknown
steps: Wash the rice in several waters, then leave it in a basin of cold water to soak for two or three hours
Have ready a saucepan full of water, with a little salt in it
When the water boils, drain the rice and put it into the saucepan
Let it boil very quickly for about seven minutes, then pour it into a colander, and place the colander on the top of the saucepan, that the water may quite drain off
The rice ought to be stirred with a fork that the grains may be separated
It ought to be boiled in a large quantity of water, and it will be sufficiently cooked when the grains become a little soft, and over done if they at all stick together
Rice should always be served in a separate dish from the currie

name: Torta de Pies de Puerco (Pork Feet Cake)
author: Mariano Galván Rivera
ingredientsText: molleja or liver, or small fish pieces
steps: When the pork feet are half-cooked, add a hen so that everything finishes cooking together.
Skim the broth and add salt, all spices, ground garlic, and chorizos.
Do this the day before the cake is to be eaten.
On the day it is to be served, make a picadillo with all its requisites, adding four to six beaten eggs stirred so they are set, and a little saffron.
To the broth in which the hen cooked, well seasoned with all spices, add a little vinegar.
Beat ten to twelve eggs separately, beating first the whites and then adding the yolks.
Put the picadillo in a pan over the fire, gradually adding sliced tongue, pieces of pork feet without bones, hen, chorizo, sliced hard-boiled eggs, raisins, almonds, olives, and capers.
Pour this over half the beaten egg in a pan with very hot lard so it sets, doing so carefully so the pieces of picadillo do not mix with the egg.
After adding the picadillo, cover it completely with the other half of the beaten egg.
When recognized with a knife that the cake is set, lower it to the ground by placing a comal on top so it cooks without lard.
When well browned, if the pan is not full, add more well-puffed beaten eggs and put the comal on top again.
If there is suspicion that the cake is not well cooked, put it back on gentle fire until it is.

For the sauce, fry from morning twelve ground tomatoes with garlic, chiles, and parsley, then adding a little broth, eight egg yolks, and the juice of two lemons, stirring quickly so the yolks break down.
Let it simmer for a while and add all spices and more well-washed capers, or in their place molleja or small liver pieces, or small fish pieces, mint, parsley, and saffron.
When bringing to the table, add olives and any other garnishes desired.
sourceTitle: Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano

name: Wine Vapor Duck
author: Shiu Wong Chan
steps: Open the ducks with one cut about 4 inches long in the back of each.
When the ducks have been cleaned, place them in a suitable bowl with the back upward.
Rub the duck inside and out with spicery salt.
Place carefully in each duck one of the cups of wine. Be sure the wine does not spill on the duck.
Steam in a double-boiler for 2½ hours, or until tender.
Remove cover. Pour in cold water to stop the steam. By means of a cloth take out the cups of wine.
Pour off the gravy into another bowl. Skim off the oil.
Place over the bowl containing the duck a second bowl a little larger than the first. Turn the first bowl upside down so that the duck falls into the second bowl.
Now pour the gravy back over the duck. Garnish with the Chinese ham cut into small oblong pieces and with a little parsley.

name: Yohan Candy
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
steps: Boil adzuki (purple beans) to a paste, and mix with sugar and seaweed gelatine.
Allow it to harden.
